_comment: Guided tour for CLSM Pixel Select. Steps point at real controls; the ones with an await wait until the user presses the control.

steps.title: What this tool does
steps.text:
A confocal lifetime scan is a photon stream with markers for frames, lines and pixels. This tool rebuilds the images from it, lets you paint pixels on an image and shows the photon decay of exactly those pixels.

Seven steps; you press the buttons, the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Open the photons
steps.text: Open TTTR / imaging reads a PTU (or HT3) scan; the scanner markers are detected from its header and filled into Acquisition.

await.hint: Press Open TTTR / imaging and choose a file.

steps.title: Check the acquisition settings
steps.text: Detector channels chooses which routing channels are summed; the markers and pixels per line normally need no change for a scan from the supported scanners.

steps.title: Build the image
steps.text: Build CLSM reconstructs a scanner image from the photons and the settings.

steps.title: A representation to look at
steps.text: Add representation computes the intensity (or the mean micro-time) image you paint on; Image type in Brush & Decay chooses which.

steps.title: Paint a decay
steps.text: Drag with the left mouse button over the image to select pixels (the middle button pans). With Live update the decay of the painted pixels appears below as you paint.

steps.title: Keep what you found
steps.text: Add decay -> ChiSurf publishes the decay as an experimental dataset for fitting; Export decay CSV and Export image write files. Press Help for the representations and the brush.
